Sports.title: Chelsea consider shock move for England centre back John Stones, 32, after his Man City exit
Sports.content:
Chelsea are considering a move for John Stones after his release by Manchester City following the expiry of his contract.

The 32-year-old central defender is available on a free this summer, and is now enjoying downtime after representing England at the World Cup, including starting in their semi-final exit to Argentina.

Chelsea’s interest comes a month after club sources tried to kill off rumours circulating within football circles that they were looking at Stones. However, he is now a legitimate candidate, it can be confirmed.

Chelsea have benefited from having experienced heads in defence before, such as Thiago Silva. However, Arsenal have also been linked with Stones, who is reportedly seen as a possible short-term option if William Saliba’s injury proves serious.

Chelsea have been in talks for Maxence Lacroix, with negotiations even held at ownership level in a meeting between Behdad Eghbali and Steve Parish at a hotel in New York.

John Stones played in five of England's World Cup matches, including the agonising semi-final exit to Argentina

Palace want around £60million for the 26-year-old who was with France at the World Cup. Como’s Jacobo Ramon, 21, is also a candidate who has featured on Chelsea’s shortlist for some time.

While chasing at least one central-defender signing, Chelsea have long maintained that their highly-rated academy graduate Josh Acheampong is not for sale despite multiple approaches.

However, the 20-year-old would be forgiven for wondering whether he will receive meaningful minutes in the upcoming season, with Chelsea having fallen out of European football. Sources close to Acheampong believe he is ready to play.

Chelsea are scheduled to fly to Sydney, Australia at the end of this week to begin their pre-season tour under Xabi Alonso. The club have not yet confirmed their travelling squad.

Chelsea are still waiting for several of their World Cup representatives to return with players entitled to three-week breaks. Some with loan options, particularly among the youngsters from Cobham, could also be left at home to focus on finalising that opportunity.

Sports.title: West Ham accept £68m bid from Al-Hilal for Crysencio Summerville... with Premier League clubs now unlikely to compete at that price
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have agreed a £68million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long-term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, Netherlands international Summerville was on Manchester United's radar and they held exploratory talks with West Ham.

Summerville joined the Hammers from Leeds for £25m in the summer of 2024 and scored eight goals in 56 games for the club but was unable to help them avoid relegation to the Championship last season.

West Ham are still looking to offload Jean-Clair Todibo, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Alphonse Areola, Edson Alvarez and Niclas Fullkrug.

Al-Hilal have agreed a £68million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville

With Aston Villa progressing on Alejandro Garnacho talks, Roma are now likely to look at RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, who also figured lower down on Arsenal's list, and his Norway compatriot Andreas Schjelderup at Benfica. Diego Moreira at Strasbourg has also been floated.

Sports.title: Inside Michael Carrick's Man United revolution: How Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos take team to next level, latest on search for another midfield star, the Lisandro Martinez issue and academy talents pushing for first-team spot
Sports.content:
Inside Michael Carrick's Man United revolution: How Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos take team to next level, latest on search for another midfield star, the Lisandro Martinez issue and academy talents pushing for first-team spot

Unlock more from our team inside the Man United camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

As Manchester United’s players and staff left Helsinki’s Olympic Stadium on Saturday, there was disappointment at a 1-0 defeat by Wrexham – but also excitement at what a full season under Michael Carrick will look like.

The pre-season opener was the moment to dust off the cobwebs. United are not at full tilt with some key pieces of the Carrick puzzle still on their post-World Cup holidays, and many of the club’s best young academy players are continuing to jockey for a spot in the squad when the season commences.

New midfielder Andrey Santos is already said to be impressing team-mates with his intensity in training, while goalkeeper Karl Darlow, nursing a small injury after a procedure at the back end of last season, and Youri Tielemans, on a post-World Cup break, are still to come in and make their mark.

But United’s transfer business is far from done. Carrick and his staff are still keen on a third midfielder, want to ease the load on Benjamin Sesko up top, and are targeting a left-sided addition (it is still to be decided if that is a left winger or left back).

The manager's revolution is still gathering momentum. Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the state of play ahead of this week’s second pre-season friendly against Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim on Friday.

Manager Michael Carrick knows there is still plenty to be done at Manchester United ahead of the new season

WHAT’S THE LATEST WITH DEFENDERS?

United need to assess the extent of the injury suffered by Lisandro Martinez in the World Cup final before deciding if a new centre back needs boosting up the shopping list.

Matthijs de Ligt is set to miss the start of the season while he recovers from back surgery, leaving Harry Maguire, Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro as the only senior centre back options.

United feel well stocked at right back with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, both of whom can play on the left too, but Carrick is keen to have a reliable ball-playing centre back in his line-up to help break the lines, something Martinez excels at.

The two have a very close relationship and the extent of Martinez’s injury issue is likely to put significant weight on whether a new central defender – United were keen on Murillo before he signed a new deal with Nottingham Forest – is back on the agenda.

Left back is a position higher up the priority list, largely because Luke Shaw starting every game last season has to be seen as an anomaly, as positive as it was.

Left back Harry Amass is determined to leave a lasting impression during pre-season and was among the stand-outs for United in Helsinki. But there is significant Championship interest in him and the feeling is that a late move will be sanctioned, particularly if Patrick Dorgu’s role is re-allocated from wing back to full back.

A nugget of information from academy circles: there is A-League interest from Australia in rising star full-back James Overy, while Rangers are also monitoring him. One to watch.

Left back Harry Amass in action for United against Wrexham on Saturday. The 19-year-old is determined to impress during pre-season

United need to ascertain the extent of the injury sustained by Lisandro Martinez during the World Cup final

WHAT NEXT FOR THE MIDFIELD REBUILD?

This is the defining area of the pitch for United to get right and has been the focus of months and months of meetings by Ineos and the decision-makers at Old Trafford.

Carrick wants United to play with greater control next season so they can dominate matches and not rely on playing in transition, which they did effectively for so much of his time in charge last term.

Casemiro and Kobbie Mainoo worked well as a partnership but the emphasis at United this summer has been to find a combination of midfielders who can disrupt their opponents while also being able to dictate from a deeper base.

United’s top target was Elliot Anderson before that move became too much of a stretch financially and he went to Manchester City for £116million. Similarly Mateus Fernandes, whom many inside United were convinced would join, went to Tottenham Hotspur for £85m.

Those missed targets ultimately led them back to a player who they wanted when Alejandro Garnacho went to Chelsea, and another that figures inside United believe could be the pound-for-pound signing of the season.

Santos was requested by United as part of the Garnacho deal, only for Chelsea to shoot that down. But now they have their man. And the Brazil international is viewed as someone who has the natural instincts to play as a No 6, a more defensive screening midfielder, in front of the defence. He is expected to provide the midfield protection that was severely lacking in the final knockings of the Erik ten Hag era, and often a bone of contention during Ruben Amorim's reign.

Then there is Youri Tielemans. United activated his £35m release clause, a deal they desperately tried to keep under wraps as part of a concerted effort to do their business in the shadows and away from the media.

The Belgian is Premier League proven, a player United believe can dictate matches, and should ease the creative burden on Bruno Fernandes in front of him.

United hope that Youri Tielemans will bring the control to United's midfield that was lacking last season

United still want a third midfielder and they hold interest in Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi, among others

United still want a third midfielder and they hold interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott, who declined to sign a new contract on Tuesday, Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi, Roma's Manu Kone, Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid and Fulham's Sander Berge - and this is the signing that stylistically should tell us a lot about Carrick’s United.

The expectation is that he will stick with the 4-2-3-1 system that served him so well last season, allowing Fernandes to flourish as the No 10, with two players, one more defensive than the other, at the base of midfield.

But a move for Scott, over say, Kone, would allow United to hold the tactical flexibility for a more ball-dominant 4-3-3 that Paris Saint-Germain, for example, have used to great effect.

United sources have been more tight-lipped than ever about Ineos' thinking, but what is abundantly clear is United won’t overpay for players, won’t pay enormous wages, and want to continue to pull rabbits out of the hat just when you think you’ve figured out their next move.

IS CARRICK SETTLED ON HIS GOALKEEPERS?

Yes. Senne Lammens is his No 1 and there are no question marks about the Belgian despite his costly error against Spain in their World Cup quarter-final.

Team-mates, including fellow goalkeeper Tom Heaton, have already reached out to Lammens and the sense inside the United camp is that the summer adversity can actually make him a better goalkeeper in the long run, to United’s benefit.

Landing a back-up goalkeeper early in the summer was seen as essential and the free agent move for Darlow frees up Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek to depart.

Depending on who you speak to at United, some sources believe a realistic fee for Vitek comes in at around £15m, with the Czech shot-stopper open to leaving permanently, which appears, as of now, to be United’s preferred route.

‘I'm ready to go somewhere again and hopefully be No 1,’ Vitek told a few of us after the Helsinki match. ‘There has been a few (clubs) on the table. We're hoping to choose the best one and hopefully it will happen soon.’

‘I'm ready to go somewhere again and hopefully be No 1,’ United's Radek Vitek said after the Wrexham match

There is a sense inside the United camp that his World Cup adversity can actually make Senne Lammens a better goalkeeper in the long run

The move to keep Heaton around was seen as imperative by all because of his experience and his leadership in the dressing room; a key conduit between the players and staff.

The goalkeepers are set: 1. Lammens. 2. Darlow. 3. Heaton.

ANY YOUNGSTERS WHO CAN CHIP IN?

Simply put, United have too many young players that have outgrown academy football but are also not ready to be thrust into the first team.

There are a lot of youngsters determined to find a role for themselves in the squad for next season, not least with United’s budget unable to stretch to refreshing every position, but also because Carrick and his staff have an immense amount of data on each of them.

Amass is particularly interesting at left back, while midfielder Jacob Devaney, who shone out on loan with St Mirren, is among those fighting to be the additional midfielder promoted from the academy for the coming season.

Tyler Fletcher has loan interest from Kilmarnock but wants to stay and fight for his place, while others such as Sekou Kone (Lausanne), Jack Moorhouse (countless options across League One, as well as abroad), and Jack Fletcher (lots of EFL loan interest) are expected to play elsewhere.

Chido Obi did not get on in Helsinki and there is a degree of uncertainty about the next best move for him. Some inside United are reluctant to send him out on loan but there is also an acknowledgement that he needs to be tested after spending the entirety of last season in the academy set-up.

Cristian Orozco, the physical defensive midfielder who has arrived from Fortaleza after turning 18, will start with the club’s Under 21s before being assessed for his suitability to be in and around the first team. David Eze and Karim Cassim are two Man City youth players United are focused on acquiring this summer as part of their aggressive academy recruitment drive, too.

Tyler Fletcher has loan interest from Kilmarnock but wants to stay and fight for his place

Midfielder Jacob Devaney is fighting to be the additional midfielder promoted to the first team from the academy for the coming season

HOW IS THE LEFT WING LOOKING?

The £8m signing of Tynan Thompson only added to the intrigue around what is happening on the left wing.

Thompson has joined from Tottenham Hotspur as an Emerging Talent Signing, similar to the 2025 deal for Heaven, which has since proved a steal. While Thompson will have to earn a shot at the first team, a key part of the vision sold to the player was that the pathway is right in front of him, as evidenced by Heaven.

Speaking to one key figure in the England player pathway, Daily Mail Sport was told that Thompson is a ‘United-type winger from the 90s’ who will bring a strong one-versus-one ability which has been missing off the left across United’s academy sides.

Adding to the left wing conundrum is the fact Marcus Rashford and his £325,000-a-week contract remains on the books after Barcelona passed up on the chance to sign him, while Dorgu has been viewed as a winger, rather than a left back option, under Carrick.

Noah Ajayi, a 17-year-old who is one of the academy’s brightest players and was in line to play a part in pre-season until an ankle injury put paid to that, needs to see a pathway is there for him, too, amid interest from top clubs in Germany, Italy and Portugal.

Interest in West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, who is now bound for Saudi Arabia, was dependent on any potential exit for Rashford, while the role of Dorgu further complicates recruitment. Should Rashford, who doesn’t have an allocated squad number at United right now, be fully reintroduced, he will expect to be a major factor out on the left.

The £8million signing of Tynan Thompson from Spurs only adds to the intrigue around what will happen on the left wing for United

All of which is tied up in the future of £325,000-a-week Marcus Rashford, whom Barcelona have declined to sign

IS ANOTHER CENTRE FORWARD AN OPTION?

Sesko’s shin injury is a lingering problem for United and there is a real lack of depth up top. Matheus Cunha is capable in that position, as is Bryan Mbeumo, and Carrick does like the false-nine approach, particularly in games where United are not expecting to dominate the ball.

United are open to moving on Joshua Zirkzee but he is one of the most popular members of the dressing room and is eager to fight for his place with more games available now United are back in Europe.

Sports.title: Ben Earl is right to call Nations Championship 'brutal'. It's pushing players to breaking point, and England are suffering unfairly. But here's why it's here to stay despite World Rugby's vow, writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Ben Earl hasn’t always hit the nail on the head.

In March, after England were beaten by Italy for the first time in Six Nations history, the forward’s comment that his team ‘played pretty well’ was at best wide of the mark and at worst badly deluded. This time, however, Earl isn’t wrong.

His assessment of England’s summer schedule as ‘brutal’ and his call for Nations Championship reform were refreshingly honest and a rare example of a leading figure in Test rugby being prepared to say it as it is.

Over the course of the past three weeks, England have played South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in Johannesburg, Liverpool and Santiago del Estero respectively. Three matches, three consecutive Saturdays, three different continents. Miles travelled? 25,000. Number of flights? Eight. No wonder the players are knackered.

‘It's been brutal. There's no two ways about it,’ England No 8 Earl said. ‘It's been tough coming at the end of what's been quite a long season anyway. It has seemed a bit weird but it's just something we're going to have to get used to because it's just the beginning. We just get told where to go and where to play.’

Unfortunately, Earl is right there, too.

Ben Earl gives his all during his side's victory over Argentina on Saturday, England's third match in as many weeks on three different continents

Tom Curry, Luke Cowan-Dickie, Marcus Smith and Tommy Freeman of England enjoy a well-earned sit down after the win over Argentina

It is unlikely the Nations Championship – which was introduced for the first time this summer and will conclude in November – is going anywhere. It is slated to take place biannually and the £90million broadcast deal its organisers struck with ITV has undoubtedly raised significant revenue for the game.

But at what cost to those who take to the field? Asking players such as Earl to finish what has already been a tough campaign by flogging themselves around the world simply does not marry up with World Rugby’s claim that player welfare is their ‘No 1 priority’. If it was, the players would be looked after better. Good on Earl for calling out this important issue.

Other players and coaches have failed to do so, afraid of rocking the boat and antagonising the Six Nations and SANZAAR (a consortium of the South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina governing bodies), who run the new competition.

The Nations Championship has been introduced as a means of packaging traditional summer and autumn fixtures into a cross-hemisphere competition, replacing traditional tours. The next set of fixtures will take place across Europe in November and will conclude with a finals weekend at Twickenham.

I believe there is sporting merit in the tournament. However, on the evidence of the first three rounds, it is asking too much of the players. Further, it is clear that the demands are tougher for those from the northern hemisphere.

The travel demands England have been put through this summer have been significant, the huge amount of time spent in the air leaving Steve Borthwick’s side little time to train ahead of the rigours of Test rugby. They have not been the only ones. Wales have been from Cardiff to Argentina and then South Africa. How can you expect players to perform at their best on such a schedule?

It’s impossible. When New Zealand arrive in the north this November, they will face Scotland, Wales and England. For South Africa, it’s Italy, France and Ireland. No long-haul flights between games. It is clearly not a level playing field for the 12 competing teams.

‘Why would we not all be playing in one country?’ Earl said. ‘So, you just don't travel, you go to one nation and have that festival feel. But I'm not paid to make those decisions.’

Noah Caluori scores against Fiji for England who have been flying here, there and everywhere over the last three weeks

England started off their Nations Championship with a tough match against South Africa at altitude in Johannesburg

Earl’s suggestion is sensible, but unlikely to happen for commercial reasons - countries won't give up home internationals lightly when sponsors have paid big bucks to be seen.

When Daily Mail Sport raised concerns about the Nations Championship’s logistics and player welfare back in February, we were given a rebuke from its organisers. We were told the demands weren’t higher than previous years, that travel concerns had been listened to and that support – such as chartered planes – had been laid on. The message was clear – nothing to see here.

But now stars such as Earl have spoken up, things are different. Without the players, there is no game and too much is being asked of rugby’s top commodity.

Maro Itoje and Tommy Freeman have both exceeded English rugby’s 30-game-a-season limit in the past. Itoje had to be rested totally this summer. Henry Slade passed the 30-match cap in the season just finished. Earl finished 2025 with the Lions in Australia on August 2. This year, it was July 19 in the backwaters of Argentina.

Earl and his team-mates will now get five weeks off to try to recuperate before going to the well again. But it is not sustainable in the long-term. Earl has put the ball in the court of rugby’s organisers - and good on him. But will his concerns be heard?

You really have to hope so.

Sports.title: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor announces retirement aged 47 - with Englishman bowing out after officiating at this summer's World Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League referee Anthony Taylor announces retirement aged 47 - with Englishman bowing out after officiating at this summer's World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from refereeing aged 47 ending his career at the World Cup.

The Englishman's last match as a referee was eventual World Cup champions Spain's last-16 1-0 win over Portugal on July 6.

Taylor's career as an official saw him involved in 831 matches which spanned over two decades.

During that time he was a Premier League referee for 16 seasons, being the man in the middle on 432 occasions.

Aside from the Premier League, he officiated the 2024 Champions League final as Real Madrid beat Borussia Dortmund, the FA Cup final in 2017 and 2020, the 2015 League Cup final and the 2018 Championship play-off final.

As well as this summer's World Cup, he officiated the 2022 World Cup in Qatar as well as the 2020 and 2024 European Championships.

Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from refereeing, bowing out at the World Cup

Explaining why he is retiring, Taylor cited the demands of the job.

'Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant,' Taylor said in a statement.

'The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.

'I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years. Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.'

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, English football's professional refereeing body, said of Taylor: 'He's consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it's not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many.

'The professionalism he's shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.'

Sports.title: Aston Villa propose loan move with obligation to buy for Alejandro Garnacho - with Chelsea wanting £40m permanent deal
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell-on percentage.

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add-ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister's father firmly denies Real Madrid talks amid speculation Liverpool star had 'offered himself' to Spanish giants
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister's father has firmly shut down speculation of a potential move for his son to Real Madrid, according to reports.

The Liverpool star has enjoyed a strong World Cup campaign with Argentina, reaching the final before defeat to winners Spain on Sunday afternoon.

But as Mac Allister prepares to return to his club after a well-deserved break, his father Carlos has been quick to stamp out suggestions that he is set for a new season away from Anfield.

Spanish media first hinted at a potential move this week, with Defensa Central claiming that Mac Allister and his representatives had offered him to Real Madrid.

But speaking to online outlet 365scores, the elder Mac Allister left no room for misinterpretation.

'We have not spoken with any official at Real Madrid,' his statement read. 'What is being circulated about us holding talks with Real Madrid is not true.

Alexis Mac Allister is not thought to be agitating for a move to Real Madrid, according to his father Carlos

'Mac Allister is still under contract for two seasons at Liverpool, and currently he will get some rest for a few days, and then return to play in the Premier League, and that is the current situation.'

Mac Allister has featured for the Merseyside club since his move from Brighton in 2023, but Real Madrid has had a sharp-elbowed summer in the market so far.

As well as prising former coach Jose Mourinho away from Benfica ahead of the World Cup, the Spanish giants inked a £60million deal to bring Marc Cucurella to the capital from Chelsea.

Mac Allister's team-mate Ibrahima Konate has also made the move to LaLiga with Los Blancos, departing Liverpool as a free agent.

Real Madrid have similarly secured former Manchester City midfielder Bernardo Silva, while Denzel Dumfries was tempted away from Inter Milan after the club activated his £17.1m release clause.

Carlos previously acted as his son's spokesperson in April 2025, when Real Madrid previously appeared to be circling the Premier League winner.

Mac Allister had given a vague response to a question posed by AS suggesting that he could see himself playing in Spain 'one day' due to the country's similarity to his own.

Then, Carlos squashed the potential for rumours to blossom saying: 'Alexis is very happy where he is.'

Mac Allister was among the 16 national team players who returned to Buenos Aires after losing their World Cup final, with missing team-mates opting to return to their clubs or begin their holidays from the USA or Europe.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr says Glasgow 2026 will be 'much more of a fun time' after world record
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr says Glasgow 2026 will be 'much more of a fun time' after world record

Josh Kerr, who is from Edinburgh, had a 'Commonwealth Games hopeful' T-shirt as a teenager. He told of his early career before he races for Scotland at Glasgow 2026.

View 2 Images BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND - AUGUST 04: Josh Kerr of Team Scotland reacts after competing in the Men's 1500m Round 1 heats on day seven of the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games at Alexander Stadium on August 04, 2022 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

World record holder Josh Kerr was given a "Commonwealth Games hopeful" T-shirt as a teenager.

He told the story of his early career as he returns to Scotland to compete in Glasgow 2026, the biggest UK sporting event of the summer.

At just 13, Kerr tried different events at the main Games venue, including shot put and high jump.

‌



In July 2011, almost 15 years to the day that he will run the Commonwealth Mile, the record books show Kerr ran 4m 30.91 as a 13-year-old.

He also threw the shot 7m 34cm and did a 1m 55cm high jump.

Aldi worker swaps aisles for Scotland boxing team at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

View 2 Images Oliver Hoare of Team Australia and Josh Kerr of Team Scotland compete during the Men's 1500m Round 1 heats on day seven of the Birmingham 2022

The Glasgow 2026 gold medal contender cut his teeth racing at tracks around Scotland.

And he was no stranger to the Scotstoun Stadium where the Athletics and Para Athletics events will be held from Thursday.

Now that young “hopeful” is running 3mins 42.66 for the mile and is keen to win gold in Glasgow and put on a show for his home crowd.

‌



Kerr recalled: “I grew up in youth academies for future Commonwealth Games hopefuls, and that will never leave me.

"I still have the 'Scottish Commonwealth Games hopeful' T-shirt. It was a bit rough back then but there’s definitely a lot of memories held in it.

"So, to be able to go out there and represent my country in front of a home crowd at the Commonwealth Games, that's all I want for my career.”

‌



Athletics and Para Athletics events will take place over six days at Scotstoun Stadium from July 27 to August 1, with 59 gold medals up for grabs.

The Men’s and Women’s Mile finals are run on August 1 with a small number of tickets remaining in the heats, on 29 July and 30 July.

Kerr will spearhead a strong field in the “Commonwealth Mile” alongside fellow Scots Jake Wightman and Neil Gourley.

‌



He added: “Now it's time to race the best guys in the Commonwealth. So, I'm not too worried about times right now.

"I'm not battling machines and battling personalities, so it'll be a much more of a fun time.

"I think that would be one way of capping off a great couple of weeks.”

Fans are encouraged not to miss out and get their hands on their tickets, available at glasgow2026.com/tickets.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will both take part in warm-up fights later this week, and one boxing legend has revealed why fans should not be worried ahead of their clash later this year

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are both expected to come away without a scratch in their warm-up fights, finally setting up a long-awaited showdown.

‌



That is according to boxing legend Teddy Atlas - who expects the heavyweight icons to 'wipe the floor' with their respective opponents. Joshua will make a sensational return to the ring on Saturday night - seven months on after being involved in a horrific car crash just days after knocking out Jake Paul.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on unknown fighter Kristian Prenga over in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. But just over 24 hours before Joshua makes the walk to the ring, Fury is expected to have a tune-up fight of his own. The 'Gypsy King' will meet Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand.

‌



Providing both men win, they will meet later this year. The pair finally agreed to a fight earlier this year, and are expected to settle their 10-year feud in November. While Prenga has vowed to scupper those plans, Atlas is expecting a relatively easy night at the office for both Fury and 'AJ' later this week.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

In an interview with CanadaCasino, he said: "I think the warm-up fights are pretty much foregone conclusions. I’m not knocking anyone who gets in the ring, but in a practical sense, they are foregone conclusions. Wach is 46 years old and has been knocked out five times. With Joshua and Prenga, I think it is all up to Joshua and how long the fight goes. But we don’t know where Joshua is emotionally coming off that near-fatal car accident. We don’t know how that has impacted him. We saw how a car accident may have impacted Errol Spence.

"With Joshua, I definitely tell you it has impacted him. I just don’t know how much and how. If he is in a halfway decent place, I think he goes behind the jab, catches Prenga and the fight is over, maybe in two rounds. If he is not, maybe he does not do anything for a few rounds and allows Prenga to survive. But at the end of the day, there should only be one guy left standing, and it should be Joshua."

Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Fans are chomping at the bit to see both Joshua and Fury trade leather, but Atlas believes the fight has been made far too late, seeing as both men have lost multiple times over the last few years. "It’s definitely a money grab," he said. "Joshua is two fights on from being knocked out badly against Dubois, Fury has lost a couple of times to Usyk, and both of them have lost their most significant fights of recent times. There is no arguing that both of them have slippage in their performances and in their careers at this point in their lives. They are not spring chickens anymore. They have been in tough fights, and it shows.

Article continues below

"Ali and Frazier in Manila were too late. Their skills had been eroded, they had been diminished, but it became one of the great heavyweight fights because they were more available to each other than they would have been when their skills were sharper. The one thing that was not diminished was their character, their resolve, their determination and their championship qualities. So yes, Fury vs Joshua is late, and yes, it’s a money grab, but it still might give you some of that because they’re heavyweights.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job

Gianni Infantino has come under fire following a controversial World Cup with the FIFA president told one outcome changing could have resulted in him being dismissed

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been sent a damning World Cup message (Image: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

La Liga president Javier Tebas has admitted Gianni Infantino could have lost his job at FIFA if the USA beat Belgium in the World Cup last-16. The build up to that clash was engulfed in controversy after USA star Folarin Balogun had his red card from the previous knockout round against Bosnia and Herzegovina suspended for 12 months.

‌



U.S. President Donald Trump called Infantino regarding the incident, with FIFA's disciplinary committee later reversing the decision to make him available to manager Mauricio Pochettino again. Despite his inclusion, the co-host nation were comfortably beaten 4-1 and Tebas has stated that result likely saved Infantino his job as president.

‌



During an interview with Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport, Tebas said: "The suspension of the American player's ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky that Belgium eliminated the USA, because otherwise a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job."

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

He could have potentially lost his job regardless with an official complaint made to The International Olympic Committee that his dealings with Trump breached political neutrality. However, he will not face any sanctions from the IOC, of which he has been a member of for the last six years.

Infantino's role as FIFA president is still under increasing pressure though, with Tebas the latest high-profile figure to speak out against the 56-year-old.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up," he said. "There's no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. He shouldn't stay, but the current state of affairs means he won't leave."

Though the next World Cup is not until 2030, it has been in the headlines with Infantino and FIFA'S vice president Alejandro Dominguez open to a 64-team tournament. Tebas, who was in the United States to watch his country lift the trophy this year, has explained why he thinks that is not a good idea.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has spoken out against Gianni Infantino

‌



He said: "Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense. The football industry isn't just the World Cup. It's the national competitions that sustain this sport. They are destroying the football industry, which generates tens of thousands of jobs, for an event that lasts 40 days and involves a minority of players.

"Are the best players there? Clearly, but they are also in our leagues. We need fewer international matches and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don't realise they are making irresponsible decisions."

One positive of the proposed format would be that 16 groups of four teams would not see any third-placed teams get through but the round of 32 would remain. A record 104 matches were played across the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer. That would jump up to 128 if FIFA got their wish of expanding the World Cup.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss

Argentina suffered a painful defeat in Sunday's World Cup final to Spain and first-choice keeper Emi Martinez has admitted he is now considering his future with the national team

View 2 Images Emi Martinez has indicated he is contemplating international retirement (Image: Juan Mabromata/AFP)

Emi Martinez has revealed that is considering his international future following Argentina's loss in the World Cup final, saying he must decide whether it is now "time to step aside".

‌



The Aston Villa goalkeeper was a colossus in Argentina's triumph in Qatar four years ago during an epic penalty shootout victory over France and again on Sunday, where he kept Spain at bay until extra-time. Ferran Torres eventually beat Martinez to deny Argentina the chance to make history with successive World Cup titles.

‌



Martinez is the latest Argentina star to send a message to supporters on social media after the heartbreaking defeat.

‌



And the 33-year-old, who has won 67 caps for his country, has hinted that Sunday's game in New Jersey could end up being his final international appearance.

FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced READ MORE :

“I dreamt we'd win it again, I dreamt of bringing it back to Argentina and making history once more,” Martinez wrote in a post on Instagram.

“The truth is, the pain is hard to explain. There are many things to reflect on and how to move forward, and if it's time to step aside.

‌



“I'm so sorry, I truly tried my best to help my country and my team-mates.”

Argentina and Martinez were left up against it when the Chelsea midfielder, Enzo Fernandez, was shown a red card in the final minutes of regulation time. They eventually succumbed to Spanish pressure in extra-time but had been under the pump all game, failing to register a single effort on goal until the 116th minute.

View 2 Images Martinez helped Argentina win the World Cup in 2022 with crucial penalty saves against France (Image: Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



The aftermath of the game was marred by ugly scenes as Argentine frustration boiled over, with Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes both lashing out at opponents.

Their behaviour was condemned by Wayne Rooney, who argued that their conduct in previous games hardly made their poor reaction a surprise. The BBC pundit said: “Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this with Argentina before.

“It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them.”

Sports.title: Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, set to make first-team debut THIS week as ban lifted
Sports.content:
Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, set to make first-team debut THIS week as ban lifted

Manchester United star JJ Gabriel has been on the verge of a first-team breakthrough for some time and it appears that the teenager could finally be in line to make his senior debut

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has been unable to make a first-team appearance yet (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel is set to make his long-awaited first-team debut in the Red Devils’ clash with Rosenborg. Michael Carrick’s side take on the Norwegian side in their second pre-season friendly of the summer on Friday.

‌



A similar squad is expected to be named to the one that lost 1-0 to Wrexham, albeit with a few differences. Gabriel, 15, took part in United’s latest training session on Monday at Carrington and is under consideration to be included in the squad to fly to Norway.

‌



Taking to Instagram after the defeat to Wrexham, the teenager wrote: “The longer you wait for something the more you appreciate it when you get it because anything worth having is worth waiting for.”

‌



Gabriel has been part of United’s youth system since 2022 and has been working his way up through the ranks. In 2025, he became the youngest-ever player to represent the club’s under-18 side, while he has regularly been handed opportunities to train with the first team.

He also enjoyed a brilliant season last term, having scored 26 goals in 29 appearances for United’s youth team last season as they reached the FA Youth Cup final. Gabriel has yet to make his first-team debut due to a rule about player ages, albeit he can sign a professional deal when he turns 17 in October next year.

Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars READ MORE :

Speaking about Gabriel last season, Carrick said: "He's not allowed [to make his debut], he's too young. He's doing really well, JJ.

‌



“We've got some really good young players in the academy and we try and get the younger players up [with the first-team] as much as we can. We're always trying to give that exposure to the players to come and train and feel it."

The United boss added: "JJ is a big talent, it's pretty obvious to know that and he's had a really good season for the U18s.

View 2 Images Gabriel trained with Man United's first team ahead of the clash with Rosenborg (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development as we do with all the different younger players and picking the right moment to step up.

"What he's done when he's trained, he's done well as you'd expect and it's good to have the younger players come up with us."

Away from Gabriel, United have added to their youth ranks over recent days by completing a deal to sign Tynan Thompson from Spurs for £4m plus £4m in add-ons.

Sports.title: FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced
Sports.content:
FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced

Plans to potentially expand the World Cup to 64 teams in the future have been heavily criticised with the chief of La Liga now taking aim at Gianni Infantino after this summer's tournament

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire during the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The president of La Liga, Javier Tebas, has accused FIFA and Gianni Infantino of trying to 'destroy football' with their plans to increase the number of teams competing at future World Cups to 64.

‌



Spain won the final of this summer's tournament on Sunday, beating Argentina 1-0 in a forgettable final. 48 teams, rather than the usual 32, competed across matches held in the United States, Canada and Mexico as part of expanded format for the first time, but Infantino has already confirmed that adding a further 16 teams will be discussed.

‌



However, Tebas has torn into the plans, claiming they make 'no sense' and that moving ahead with them would be irresponsible.

‌



“Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas told the Italian outlet, La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final READ MORE :

“The football industry is not just the World Cup, which is the most important event. But not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They are destroying the football industry, the one that generates tens of thousands of jobs for an event that lasts 40 days and to which the minority of players go.

‌



“We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise, they decide irresponsibly.”

Tebas went on to question Infantino's position following criticism of political interference at the World Cup from the United States President, Donald Trump.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has torn into Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Infantino has been in power for 10 years and is expected to be elected for a fourth term next year. But Tebas wants to see change, even if he believes it is unlikely to happen.

“In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up,” he added. “But he has the support of the system, of the federations, there is not much more to add, right?

“There is no opposition candidate, no one wants to present themselves to lose. This is the system, and it is a system that is sick at the source.

‌



“In these days here in America I have heard many people against Infantino, who do not agree with what he does. They say it, but then they do nothing.

“I don’t know if silence or complicity is worse, because those who are silent are perfectly aware of the damage that football is suffering.”

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved

The England legend was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23 before he died from cancer

Toon fans pay tribute to Kevin Keegan

Kevin Keegan was planning an emotional return to his beloved Newcastle United before his tragic death from cancer.

‌



"King Kev" was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23. He told an audience at his last appearance on Tyneside that he 'did not want a statue' like fellow Toon idols Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer. But he intended to see the "Toon army" one last time.

‌



His tragic death from cancer at 75 meant that he never got that chance. Lifelong fan Joe Black wore a Newcastle Utd shirt today which had been signed by Keegan during his personal appearance at the Tyne Theatre in Newcastle in May.

‌



View 7 Images Lifelong Newcastle United fan Joe Black with the shirt signed on his last appearance on Tyneside

He joined a stream of fans today at St James' Park who paid tribute, including his son, also Joe, 34, and his six-year-old grandson Joe. He said: "I am going to wear my shirt for the opening game of the season and then keep it and never wear it again.

"My dad was also called Joe and he was black and white daft. My first game was when I was five years old and I have been coming ever since and I am 69 now. Keegan was a hero, he was something else, and we will never forget him."

‌



Newcastle-born Carolyn Ridley, 63, also a lifelong fan, came to pay tribute and 'share stories' with supporters. He said: "He brought such great times, I still get goosebumps thinking about it. He lifted everything when he was a player and manager.

View 7 Images Kevin Keegan tributes at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We will never forget the excitement of his teams, he nearly won the league. But his football was just brilliant; I think he got the Geordies, and we got him and loved him. Every time you came here you knew you were going to see goals; he will be remembered for that and of course that TV rant."

‌



Keegan himself joked that people would remember his 'perm, his crash on TV's Superstars and his rant at Man Utd." Sir Alex Ferguson, the man famously on the other end of Keegan's "I'd love it, absolutely love it, if we beat them" tirade, said: "I had the utmost respect for him.

View 7 Images Newcastle United fan Carolyn Ridley came to pay her respects at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but I have to say the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic. He re-energised that club and brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism that great supporters can give. That's the job he did.

‌



"And he also brought three great players to the club: David Ginola, Faustino Asprilla, and Philippe Albert. I must say the challenges we had at that time were huge. It gave Newcastle - I think - their best ever team."

Fergie told Track Radio: "The best thing about him was that he held no grudges and I admired him for that." Schoolfriends Ross Hickson, 46, and Steven Porritt, of Gateshead, bumped into each other outside St James' Park.

View 7 Images Alex Ferguson said he had the 'utmost respect' for Kevin Keegan (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

‌



They shared memories of Keegan's heyday as both a player and manager. "I met him when I was 12 or 13 at the training ground," Steven, a floor layer, recalled.

"I was picking up the footballs and he said to me: 'We are £3m in debt, we can't afford to lose them'. Then he got me a ball which I got signed and took into school. He loved it up here and we loved him. I am 47 years old and could not stop crying when I heard he had died yesterday."

Ross, a courier, added: "For me, he is up there with Sir Bobby Robson as a legend of this club." Fans left floral tributes around the Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer statues at the ground.

‌



View 7 Images Shola Ameobi former Newcastle United player paid his respects to Kevin Keegan (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Former player Shola Ameobi and Newcastle Central MP Dame Chi Onwurah both came to pay their respects. One tribute read: "White roses for the Geordie from Yorkshire. You broke our hearts in 1974 but made up for it."

Another card read: 'Kevin Keegan, Angel of the North'. Others said that whatever tribute was offered 'would never be enough'. Chris Hughton, the former Toon manager, recalled Keegan's wonderful rapport with players.

‌



"He was an incredible coach. He was down to earth, charismatic, and always incredibly honest," he said. Lee Clark, now manager of Hartlepool United, played under Keegan in the 90s.

View 7 Images Fans have left tributes around the grounds of St James' Park in Newcastle (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

When he first passed his driving test, Keegan told him to take his new sports car back because he did not like the way Clark was driving it. He did the same again with Clark's next car. He said: "He was like the Pied Piper to the Geordie public. They adore him."

‌



The former BBC broadcaster Gary Richardson interviewed Keegan on many occasions. Richardson recalled completing one interview about Keegan's early life before explaining that he was returning to London. Keegan asked him to stay and they chatted for two hours.

"It was one of the greatest days of my life in broadcasting. And that is just because of the way that he was ," he added. Keegan told him that he was a 'lucky man' because all of his dreams had come true - winning the league with Liverpool, playing for England and Newcastle United, and working with the great Bill Shankly.

View 7 Images Keegan made 63 appearances for England, 31 of those as captain (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

‌



"Three days after joining Liverpool he came up to me and said 'you will play for England son," Keegan recalled. "And I never had any doubt about it because it was Bill Shankly telling me. And he did not mess around."

In a statement on behalf of Keegan's former Liverpool team mate and close friend Terry McDermott, his family said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of our dear friend, Kevin Keegan. Kevin was so much more than a teammate.

Article continues below

"He was a lifelong friend whose warmth, loyalty, humour and passion for football touched so many lives. The memories they shared, both on and off the pitch, will be treasured forever. Although Terry’s dementia means he is no longer able to express his feelings publicly, we know how much Kevin meant to him and how deeply this loss would have affected him.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with Jean, Laura, Sarah and all of Kevin’s family at this incredibly sad time. We hope they find comfort in the love and respect being shown for Kevin by so many people. Kevin was one of football’s true greats, but to Terry he was, above all, a cherished friend. He will be greatly missed and never forgotten."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
